title: Chapter 4 – The Tissue Level of Organization
notes: Tissue: group of similar cells with common origin/function.
Four basic tissues: epithelial, connective, muscle, nervous.
Cell junctions: tight, adherens, desmosomes, hemidesmosomes, gap junctions.
Epithelia: polarity (apical/basal), avascular, high regeneration, basement membrane.
Epithelial classification: simple/stratified/pseudostratified; squamous/cuboidal/columnar.
Glands: endocrine (ductless) vs exocrine (ducts); unicellular (goblet) vs multicellular.
Connective tissue: cells + extracellular matrix (fibers + ground substance); highly vascular (except cartilage, tendons).
CT fibers: collagen (strength), elastic (stretch), reticular (support).
Loose CT (areolar, adipose, reticular) vs dense CT (regular, irregular, elastic).
Cartilage types: hyaline, fibrocartilage, elastic; avascular, slow repair.
Bone tissue: compact vs spongy; osteons vs trabeculae.
Blood is a fluid connective tissue (plasma + formed elements).
Membranes: mucous, serous, cutaneous; synovial (connective-only).
Muscle tissue: skeletal (voluntary, striated), cardiac (involuntary, intercalated discs), smooth (involuntary).
Nervous tissue: neurons (excitable) + neuroglia (support).
Excitable cells generate action potentials via voltage-gated channels.
Tissue repair varies: epithelial regenerates well; muscle/nerve limited; fibrosis forms scar.
Aging: decreased repair capacity, ECM changes, elasticity loss.
Gap junctions allow ion/small molecule passage for cell communication.
Basement membrane: basal lamina + reticular lamina; anchors epithelium.
Endocrine secretions enter interstitial fluid → blood; exocrine to ducts.
Osteoblasts build bone; osteoclasts resorb bone.
Cutaneous membrane = skin (epidermis + dermis).
Intercalated discs: desmosomes + gap junctions for synchronized heart contraction.
Neuroglia types (e.g., astrocytes, oligodendrocytes) support neurons.
